title: Dense Prime Structural Boundaries
objective: Wire canonical dense GF(p) matrix packed import/export and unsubdivided default formatting to the checked bulk uint64 runtime primitives, eliminate interpreted per-entry cliffs, and add correctness plus representative performance ratchets

oracles: previous interpreted dense-prime serialization and formatting loops

handoff.summary: Dense small-prime matrices now use checked bulk runtime primitives for packed little-endian import/export and ordinary unsubdivided formatting. Trusted canonical BigUint64Array transfer remains zero-copy, while untrusted packed input is decoded and normalized modulo p. Focused tests cover every width, exact endian alignment, rectangular and empty shapes, invalid lengths and widths, overflow, trusted ownership, formatting, subdivisions, previous-loop differential oracles, and representative absolute, relative, and linear performance gates.
risks: Subdivided display intentionally retains the semantic Python formatter and is not accelerated by this change.
The private packed-import boundary now requires the checked Uint8Array representation; all repository callers obtain that representation from packed export or serialization.
next_steps: Integrate after the uint64 structural runtime dependency and retain the focused test in the integration tier.
Keep semantic display variants on explicit fallback paths unless a future checked bulk formatter models those variants directly.
